title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Payments and Settlement of a Record
content:
## The balance of a record

Each Demurrage and Detention Free Time record keeps one running balance in US dollars. Invoices and free-time extension fees raise it; payments, waivers and dispute credits lower it.

## Rules for applying a payment

- Each remittance goes to one record only, entered with the amount remitted and with the customer's remittance reference reproduced character for character.
- Payments are accepted solely on records whose status reads invoiced.
- The balance due is the ceiling for any payment: finance returns whatever is sent beyond it, which is never booked, so the amount applied is the lower of the sum remitted and the balance due.
- Among a record's payments, each remittance reference appears once at most; the payments already on that record are what the check looks at.

## Settlement

The balance coming down to 0.00, whether by payments, waivers, credits or a mix of them, settles the record, and the settlement date entered is that same day. A settled record carries no dispute still awaiting a decision: a dispute that stands as submitted keeps the record open even at a nil balance.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical figures)

| Balance due | Sum remitted | Amount booked | Balance afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300.00 | 300.00 | 300.00 | 0.00, record settles |
| 300.00 | 120.00 | 120.00 | 180.00 |
| 300.00 | 350.00 | 300.00 (50.00 returned by finance) | 0.00, record settles |

**Q: The customer quotes a reference that already appears on this record's payments. Is it booked again?**
No; a reference can appear only once among a record's payments.

**Q: A record already shows settled. Can a further payment be booked on it?**
No; payments are booked only on records showing invoiced.
